options: 'title=py&page=2'
'title=py&page=2#top'
'/books/find?title=py&page=2'
rationales: The part after the number sign is the fragment, a separate part of the address.
That is the path followed by the query; the query starts after the question mark.

items.q: urllib.robotparser reads ['User-agent: *', 'Disallow: /private/']. What does can_fetch('*', 'https://site.example/private/c') return, and what does it mean for the server?
options: False - a request to crawlers to stay out, not an access control
False - the server will refuse the request with status 403
True - can_fetch only reports whether the site is online
rationales: RFC 9309 says the rules are not a form of access authorization; the server may still answer.
can_fetch answers whether the rules allow that agent to fetch that address, and these rules do not.

items.q: The chapter downloads a file of 178,978 bytes with iter_content(100000) and writes each chunk. Which sizes are written?
options: 178978 in one piece
rationales: Two chunks hold 178,978 bytes: one full chunk and the remainder.
iter_content hands the body over in pieces of the size given, so the file is not written in one piece.

items.q: Why does the chapter call raise_for_status() right after requests.get()?
options: A failed download such as 404 is still a Response with text; the call turns it into an exception
get() already raises an exception for every status code except 200
It saves the response body to a file
rationales: get() returns a Response for a 404 as well; only a connection failure or a timeout raises on its own.
Saving is done by write() on a file opened in 'wb' mode.

items.q: A page is saved with open(name, 'wb') and f.write('café'.encode('utf-8')). What does write() return?
options: 5, the number of bytes written
4, the number of characters
'café'
rationales: The é takes two bytes in UTF-8, so four characters are five bytes.
write() returns a count, not the text.

items.q: On the chapter's example page, soup.select('#author') is called. What comes back?
options: A list with one Tag, whose get_text() is 'Al Sweigart'
One Tag, not a list
The text 'Al Sweigart' as a string
rationales: select() always returns a list of the matching elements, even when there is one.
get_text() on a Tag gives the text; select() itself returns the Tags.

items.q: A regular expression written for <a href="..."> finds no link in <a href='https://a.example/y'> and none in <a class="n" href="https://a.example/z">. What does this show?
options: HTML can be written in many valid ways, which a parser handles and a pattern does not
The regular expression has a typing mistake and a corrected pattern will do
Beautiful Soup cannot read single quotes either
rationales: Each fix handles one more variant and leaves others; the chapter advises a parser for that reason.
A parser reads both quoting styles and the extra attribute, and returns all three addresses.

items.q: 285.44 Kelvin comes back from OpenWeather. Which expression gives Celsius?
rationales: That expression converts to Fahrenheit.
Adding moves away from Celsius; zero Celsius is 273.15 Kelvin.

items.q: A call with a wrong latitude is answered with {'cod': '400', 'message': 'wrong latitude'}. What does response_data[0] do on it?
options: Raises KeyError, because the answer is a dictionary and not a list
Gives 'wrong latitude'
Gives an empty list
rationales: Index 0 is looked up as a key; the message is under the key 'message'.
An empty list is the answer for an unknown city, a different shape.

items.q: A page's only paragraph is written by JavaScript after the page loads. What do requests and Beautiful Soup find, and what finds the text?
options: An empty element; a driven browser such as Selenium or Playwright
The text, because requests runs the script
An error, because requests refuses such pages
rationales: requests downloads the HTML as the server sent it and runs no script.
requests downloads the script text without complaint; the element is simply empty.

items.q: On 2026-10-12 the chapter's searchpypi.py was run unchanged against pypi.org. requests got status 200, a page titled Client Challenge and no .package-snippet element. What did the program do?
options: Opened no tab: min(5, 0) is 0
Raised HTTPError, because the status was not 200
Opened five tabs of the challenge page
rationales: The status was 200, so raise_for_status() has nothing to raise; the page is simply not the results page.
The tabs are opened from the links found, and there were none.

items.q: The rules ['User-agent: *', 'Disallow: /search*'] are read by urllib.robotparser. Can '*' fetch https://pypi.org/search/?q=boring+stuff?
options: Yes under Python 3.14.0 to 3.14.4, no from 3.14.5
No under every Python 3.14
Yes under every Python 3.14
rationales: Before 3.14.5 the star in a path was taken literally, so the search page was allowed.
From 3.14.5 the module follows RFC 9309 and reads the star as a wildcard.
